regime_label: pre-COVID weak/insignificant; poor data; offset approximately full
rationale: Evidence beta is above the owner pre-COVID near-zero anchor because the average includes QE-heavy Fed purchase years. Treat as regime-mixed, not a stable pre-COVID settlement state.

regime_label: not an owner annual target; pre-COVID/whole-period edge
rationale: Low beta relative to whole-period owner anchor; bank expansion and Fed purchase shares are modest, with foreign private absorption high.

Close to the COVID target on a two-year volume-weighted basis: Fed purchases plus bank expansion dominate; annual 2021 is high because Fed+bank+foreign purchases exceeded net issuance and domestic nonbanks were net sellers.

regime_label: transition; owner recent/current path approximately 0.50 begins after COVID
rationale: Large divergence below owner recent path: QT begins, deposits and MMF Treasury flows are weak/negative, and bank absorption is mostly reallocation. This is a transition-state finding.
Owner-current beta is supported only after admitting the RRP-financed MMF bill-absorption extension; strict six-mode beta is near zero because banks/Fed are not positive absorbers.
Evidence falls toward the 0.34 transition anchor as ON RRP drawdown shrinks and banks resume moderate absorption; forward authority now comes from tdcest.

rationale: Post-drain D3 evidence is below 0.34 unless residual ON RRP drawdown and stronger bank expansion are included; forward authority now comes from tdcest.
